cards.text: The tribes of Israel are out claiming the land, one tribe at a time. Now we check in on the tribe of Benjamin. The Jebusites are living in Jerusalem, and they need to be driven out.

cards.question: The Benjamites drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.

cards.text: So to this day, the Jebusites live right there among the Benjamites. Friend, that's not a move-out. That's a ROOMMATE.
Next up, the house of Joseph, Joseph's descendants. They go up to attack the city of Bethel.

cards.question: The LORD is with the house of Joseph as they attack Bethel.
Before the attack on Bethel, what does the house of Joseph send?
Bethel had an older name. It was formerly known as ___.

cards.text: The spies spot a man coming out of the city. Just a guy stepping outside, and BOOM. He's got company.

cards.question: What do the spies ask the man from Bethel to show them?

answers.text: How to get into the city

cards.text: If he does, they promise to treat him kindly. So he shows them the entrance, and they put the city to the sword.

cards.question: The man who showed them the entrance to Bethel is released, along with all his family.
After Bethel falls, the man goes to the land of the Hittites. What does he do there?

cards.text: And Luz is its name to this day. The man lost his city, so he went and built himself a SEQUEL.
Now Manasseh. Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo and their villages, and Manasseh fails to drive out the people living there.

cards.question: So why are the Canaanites still sitting in those towns Manasseh was supposed to take?

answers.text: They were determined to dwell there
They had made peace with Manasseh
They were hiding in the hills

cards.question: Later, when Israel becomes stronger, what do they do with the Canaanites?

cards.text: Strong enough to put them to work, but they never drive them out completely. That's the snooze button, friend: awake enough to hit it, never actually getting UP.

Then the reports roll in from Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher and Naphtali, and they all sound the same: they fail to drive out the people of the land. Israel and the Canaanites end up living side by side, with some of the locals put to forced labor.

cards.question: Then there's the tribe of Dan, up against the Amorites. What do the Amorites do to the Danites?

answers.text: Force them into the hill country
Push them out to the coast

cards.text: They won't even let Dan come down into the plain. That's like moving into your new house and the old owners make you live in the ATTIC.
The Amorites are determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon and Shaalbim. But then the house of Joseph grows in strength.

cards.question: Once the house of Joseph grows in strength, they drive the Amorites out completely.

cards.text: They press the Amorites into forced labor instead. And the Amorites still have a border of their own, from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.
Now the scene changes. The angel of the LORD goes up from Gilgal to another place, and he has something to say.

cards.question: Speaking as 'I,' the angel of the LORD starts with what was done for Israel. What comes first?

answers.text: Brought them up out of Egypt
Gave them a king to lead them

cards.text: The angel goes on: he led them into the land promised to their fathers. And he reminds them what he said back then, that he would never break his covenant with them.

cards.question: The angel says Israel was not to make a covenant with the people of this land. Instead, they were to tear down their ___.

cards.text: Then the angel says, 'Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this you have done?' Friend, NOBODY hears 'What is this you have done?' and thinks they're about to get a raise.

cards.question: Because Israel didn't obey, what does the angel say 'I will not' do now?

answers.text: Drive out these people before them

cards.question: The angel says the people of the land will be thorns in Israel's sides, and their gods will be a snare.
When the angel of the LORD finishes speaking to all the Israelites, the people lift up their voices and ___.
The people name that place Bochim, and there they offer sacrifices to the LORD.

cards.text: Tears first, and then sacrifices to the LORD, right there at Bochim. Friend, that is one heavy day.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank asks for Bethel's former name, Luz. Nothing earlier in the walkthrough lets the baker reason this out, so the blank tests wording they haven't seen rather than meaning. Luz matters for card 12. Tell it on a story card, or ask a different question about this moment.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: the spies promise kindness, the man shows the entrance, and the city is put to the sword. Split it.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The card is mostly a list of town names joined into one awkward run-on sentence, with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads as stripped down rather than told.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'They had made peace with Manasseh' can be argued from later in the passage. In Judges 2:2 the angel says Israel was not to make a covenant with the people of the land, yet they have not obeyed, which implies such agreements were made. Replace it with an answer that is false everywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: 'The Amorites still have a border of their own' links the border in 1:36 to the forced labor in 1:35. Judges 1:36 only states where the Amorite border extended. It doesn't say how this connects to what came before.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This card only repeats what cards 14 and 15 already told: the weeping, the sacrifices and Bochim. It doesn't move the passage forward. This is the last passage in its story group, so no 'story isn't over' line is needed here either. The card can be dropped, or replaced with something that isn't a recap.

The opening card gives context from the previous passage ('The tribes of Israel are out claiming the land, one tribe at a time,' from Judges 1:1-20) but cites only Judges 1:21. One rule says facts from outside the passage carry their reference. Another says a story card cites exactly the verses it tells, no wider. The JSON has only one verses field.
findings.question: When the opening card gives context from outside the passage, how should that context be cited? Should it widen the card's verses field, go somewhere else, or need no citation if it's general?

findings.problem: In Judges 2:1-3 the angel of the LORD speaks in God's voice, and the BSB capitalizes 'My covenant' and 'My voice.' The walkthrough refers to the angel with lowercase 'he' and says 'his covenant,' which can read as the covenant belonging to the angel himself.
findings.question: When the angel of the LORD speaks as God, should Papa Dorin attribute the words and the covenant to the angel ('his covenant'), use capitalized pronouns, or phrase it as the LORD's covenant spoken through the angel?

findings.problem: The question is in present tense ('the people lift up their voices and ___'), but the answers are past tense ('wept,' 'sang,' 'cheered'), so the completed sentence is ungrammatical. The BSB word is 'wept.'
findings.question: Should a fill-in-the-blank answer match the grammar of Papa Dorin's present-tense question (for example 'weep'), or keep the BSB's exact form ('wept') with the question reworded to fit?
